title: F5 measured - the follower looks the collected input chain up under a key that never has one
summary: InputBlocksProcessor.inputBlockTrees is keyed by the ordering block the input chain sits ON. The miner reads it that way (getBestOrderingCollectedInputBlocksTransactions -> bestOrderingBlock().id, i.e. the PARENT of the block it is mining). The follower reads it by the ANNOUNCED header's own id (getCollectedInputBlocksTransactions(headerId) in ErgoNodeViewHolder.processOrderingBlock) - a block that has no tree yet. The lookup therefore returns nothing and every reconstruction runs with an EMPTY input chain.

measured.after_the_D4_order_fix: 9 of 9 post-restart ordering blocks still fell back under root_mismatch, and the planner's own diagnostic showed why: ordering_txs=1 input_chain_txs=0 on every attempt - both orders were the same list because one half was empty
measured.log_line: input_blocks: no assembly order reproduces the transactions root ... tried=[(scala, X), (candidate, X)] ordering_txs=1 input_chain_txs=0
measured.note: F5 and F12 are independent, and F12 was only visible once the chain was non-empty; both had to be addressed before a block carrying transactions could be reconstructed at all

port_response.behaviour: collected_input_txs_for_announced tries Scala's key (the announced header's id) first and falls back to the parent's - the block the chain actually sits on, and what the miner seated. A chain genuinely recorded under the announced id still wins, so settling F5 upstream needs only the fallback deleted.

upstream_action: processOrderingBlock should look the chain up under the announced block's PARENT, matching getBestOrderingCollectedInputBlocksTransactions.
controller_note: D5 goes beyond the round-2 ruling, which named only D4. It is the same shape (Scala's behaviour first, the miner's as fallback, both reportable) and the gate cannot pass without it: with an empty input chain the D4 order choice is vacuous. Flagged for confirmation.
